User story: As an admin, I want my query split into words regardless of case and extra spaces so that 'GET  mguser' and 'get mguser' find the same cmdlets.
Expected behaviour: queryTokens lower-cases the query, splits on any run of whitespace and drops empty pieces (sources.ts:34). Names are compared against lower-cased copies (search.worker.ts:42). Leading/trailing/multiple spaces produce no extra tokens; a whitespace-only query yields zero tokens and behaves like an empty query. The same tokeniser drives result-name highlighting (ResultList.tsx:155-170), so each matched token that appears literally in the name is wrapped in <mark>.
How to test: Type 'GET-MGUSER' then '  get-mguser  ' into the search input; result count and order are identical and the first row is Get-MgUser with 'get-mguser' highlighted in a <mark>. Type '   ' and confirm the full list (same count as empty query) is shown.

User story: As an admin, I want the cmdlet whose name I typed exactly to appear at the top so that I can open it immediately.
Expected behaviour: A token equal to the full lower-cased name scores 1000, the highest per-token score (search.worker.ts:102). Results are sorted by total score descending (search.worker.ts:163), so an exact match outranks any prefix match of the same token.
How to test: Search 'get-mguser' in the Graph scope; first row is Get-MgUser, ahead of Get-MgUserMessage etc.

User story: As an admin, I want names that start with what I typed ranked highly, with the closest-length name first, so that partial typing quickly lands on the right cmdlet.
Expected behaviour: If the name starts with the token, score = 800 - min(100, nameLength - tokenLength) (search.worker.ts:103): shorter names that start with the token rank higher, and the penalty caps at 100 so any prefix match (>=700) beats a noun-prefix of equal length difference and every substring match. Ties are broken by shorter name length, then by ref (source order in SOURCES, then index order) (search.worker.ts:163).
How to test: Search 'get-mgus'; rows start with Get-MgUser and continue with longer Get-MgUser* names in increasing length; no row whose name merely contains 'get-mgus' later in the name appears above a prefix row.

User story: As an admin, I want to type just the noun (e.g. 'mailbox') and see cmdlets whose noun starts with it so that I can find all verbs for an object without knowing the verb.
Expected behaviour: The noun is the lower-cased name after the first hyphen, only when the hyphen is not at position 0; names without a hyphen have an empty noun (search.worker.ts:51). If the noun starts with the token, score = 700 - min(100, nounLength - tokenLength) (search.worker.ts:104-105). Name-prefix matches take precedence over noun-prefix (checked first).
How to test: Search 'mailbox' in Exchange scope; top rows are Get-Mailbox, Set-Mailbox, New-Mailbox, etc. (noun exactly 'mailbox'), followed by longer nouns like MailboxPermission.

Feature: Substring match anywhere in the name
User story: As an admin, I want a word found inside a cmdlet name to match even if it is not at the start of the verb or noun so that I can find cmdlets by any part of their name.
Expected behaviour: If the token occurs anywhere in the lower-cased name, score = 520 - min(120, position) (search.worker.ts:106-107): earlier occurrences rank higher, floor 400. Always below prefix and noun-prefix matches.
How to test: Search 'permission'; rows like Get-MailboxPermission appear (substring in noun), ranked below any cmdlet whose noun starts with 'permission'.

User story: As an admin, I want to type 'getmguser' without the hyphen so that I can search quickly without punctuation.
Expected behaviour: Each name also has a hyphen-stripped form (search.worker.ts:14,50). The token is also stripped of hyphens; the flat comparison runs only when the token contained a hyphen or the stripped token is at least 4 chars (search.worker.ts:108-109). A hit scores 480 - min(120, position) (search.worker.ts:110-111), below a real substring match. Tokens of 1-3 chars without hyphens skip this step. A token with misplaced hyphens (e.g. 'get-mg-user') still matches via the flat form.
How to test: Search 'getmguser'; Get-MgUser is in the top results. Search 'get-mg-user'; Get-MgUser is still found.

User story: As an admin, I want slightly misspelled queries to still find cmdlets so that a typo mid-task does not return nothing.
Expected behaviour: Only for tokens of 4+ chars and only when no exact/prefix/noun/substring/flat match applied (search.worker.ts:113). fuzzy() requires the token to be an in-order subsequence of the name, adding the current contiguous run length per char (search.worker.ts:82-97). The row matches only if the score >= 45% of the perfect score n(n+1)/2; score = 120 + round(ratio*80) - min(60, nameLength - tokenLength) (search.worker.ts:115-117), i.e. between ~60 and 200, below all literal matches. Transposed letters that break subsequence order (characters missing or reordered) return 0.
How to test: Search 'get-mgusr' (dropped letter); Get-MgUser appears in results ranked below literal matches. Search 'xyzq' and confirm it returns no fuzzy rows.

User story: As an admin, I want words from a cmdlet's description to match when the name does not so that I can search by what a cmdlet does.
Expected behaviour: If no name-based rule matched and descriptions are loaded for the source, a token contained in the lower-cased description scores 60 (search.worker.ts:119), the lowest non-zero score, so description-only hits always sort below name matches. Before descriptions load (ldesc null) such rows do not match at all.
How to test: After the page settles, search a word that appears only in descriptions (e.g. 'retention'); rows whose names lack the word but whose description contains it appear after name matches.

User story: As an admin, I want every word I type to have to match so that 'user license' narrows results instead of widening them.
Expected behaviour: For each row every token is scored independently; if any token scores 0 the row is excluded (search.worker.ts:155-158). Matching rows are ranked by the sum of token scores, then shorter name, then ref (search.worker.ts:163). Tokens may match different parts (name, noun, flat, fuzzy, description).
How to test: Search 'mguser license'; every result contains both terms (e.g. Get-MgUserLicenseDetail) and none matches only one. Add a nonsense third token 'zzzz' and confirm 0 results.

Feature: Empty query lists everything in index order
User story: As an admin, I want an empty search box to show all cmdlets in the current scope so that I can browse or just filter by facets.
Expected behaviour: With zero tokens every row that passes the filters gets score 1 (search.worker.ts:154) and no sort is applied (search.worker.ts:163), so results are in source order (SOURCES order) then shard index order. The result count label omits the timing ('· N ms') when q is empty (App.tsx:152).
How to test: Clear the search box with scope 'All'; result count equals the total cmdlet count in the placeholder ('Search N cmdlets') and no ' ms' timing is shown. Type a query and the '· N ms' suffix appears.

Feature: Scope search to one source or all sources
User story: As an admin, I want to restrict searching to one product (Graph, Az, Exchange…) or search all so that results are relevant to the module I am using.
Expected behaviour: filters.source selects a Scope: 'all' covers every source, a source id covers only that source (sources.ts:53-79). The worker searches only loaded shards whose id is in the scope (search.worker.ts:148-149). Unknown or missing scope ids from the URL fall back to 'all' (sources.ts:77). Per-source scopes have placeholder 'Search N <Short> cmdlets', 'all' has 'Search N cmdlets' (sources.ts:56,68).
How to test: Open /?source=graph (or pick Graph) and search 'user'; every row is a Graph row. Open with ?source=bogus and confirm results span all sources and placeholder reads 'Search <total> cmdlets'.

Feature: Facet filters (verb, module, category, extra, has examples)
User story: As an admin, I want to filter results by verb, module, category, API version/site role and whether examples exist so that I can narrow large result sets.
Expected behaviour: A row passes only if each non-empty filter equals the row's value exactly: verb, module, category, extra, and, when examples is true, the row must have examples (search.worker.ts:123-132). Filters are applied before scoring and combine with the query (AND).
How to test: Search 'user' in Graph, set Verb=Get; all rows start with 'Get-'. Toggle 'has examples'; count drops and every opened row shows examples. Set extra=beta; all rows carry the beta tag.

User story: As an admin, I want the filter dropdowns to list the values available in my current scope so that I only pick options that exist.
Expected behaviour: Each results message carries facets computed from all rows of the scoped sources (not narrowed by query or other filters): de-duplicated, empties removed, sorted with localeCompare (search.worker.ts:134-143,165). Verbs and categories are always provided; modules and extras are provided only for a single-source scope and are empty arrays for 'all' (sources.ts:49-50,60,72).
How to test: With scope 'All', confirm module and extra filters are not offered (empty lists). Switch to Graph; module list and the extra (API version) list appear, alphabetically sorted. Type a query and confirm facet lists do not shrink.

Feature: Names-first loading, descriptions later with automatic re-rank
User story: As an admin, I want results as soon as the name index is loaded, with descriptions filling in afterwards, so that I can start searching without waiting for the larger description files.
Expected behaviour: The worker loads all name shards first (search.worker.ts:69) and answers searches once they are in. Only then does it fetch descriptions for every source (search.worker.ts:71-73). When they arrive it re-runs the latest search under the same id (search.worker.ts:76), so the client accepts it (it is still latest) and description-only matches are added and rows now include desc text. Rows fetched before descriptions arrive have desc '' (search.worker.ts:183). A description fetch failure for a source is swallowed and that source simply keeps name-only search (search.worker.ts:59-60). While no results have arrived the count reads 'Loading index…' (App.tsx:150-151).
How to test: Throttle network, load the page and type a description-only word; at first no description-only hits appear, then after desc files load the list refreshes with additional rows and row descriptions appear. Block a /a/<build>/idx/*desc* request and confirm name search still works with no error shown.

User story: As an admin, I want a clear message if the search index cannot load so that I know the site is broken rather than waiting forever.
Expected behaviour: If any source shard fetch fails (non-2xx throws 'HTTP <status> for <path>', sources.ts:24-27), Promise.all rejects, the worker logs '[psindex] index load failed' and posts a single 'load-error' with the message (search.worker.ts:77-80). Subsequent searches and requests are never answered (search.worker.ts:236,239-240); client request promises never settle (client.ts:125-128). The UI shows 'Index unavailable' as the count and a LoadFailed panel with the message in the results area (App.tsx:148-149,186).
How to test: Block one idx shard request (e.g. via devtools request blocking) and reload; count label reads 'Index unavailable' and the results pane shows the failure message containing 'HTTP'. Typing further produces no results and no errors.

Feature: Search ids and stale result dropping
User story: As an admin typing quickly, I want only the results for my latest keystroke shown so that the list never flickers back to an older query.
Expected behaviour: Each client.search increments a shared sequence and records it as latestSearch (client.ts:115-118). Results whose id differs from latestSearch are ignored (client.ts:109). In the worker, searches that queue behind the index load are dropped unless they are still the last one received (search.worker.ts:233-236). The description re-run reuses the latest id, so it replaces current results (search.worker.ts:74-76). Requests (rows/related/find) share the sequence and are matched to replies by id; each reply resolves once and is removed (client.ts:110,129-135). The latest id is exposed via client.latest for Enter-to-open (client.ts:121-123; App.tsx:143).
How to test: With slow network, type 'g', 'ge', 'get-mguser' rapidly before the index loads; only one result set arrives and it is for 'get-mguser' (first row Get-MgUser).

User story: As an admin, I want large result lists to scroll smoothly so that browsing tens of thousands of cmdlets stays fast.
Expected behaviour: Results carry only an Int32Array of refs ((sourceIndex << 20) | rowIndex), transferred without copying (search.worker.ts:6-7,25-26,164-165). The list asks the worker for 'rows' only for the visible window (ResultList.tsx:96-101); the worker decodes each ref into a full Row with key, source, name, verb, module, category, extra, file, moduleVersion, perms, examples, desc and dup (search.worker.ts:168-186,220).
How to test: Clear the query in 'All' scope and scroll quickly to the bottom; rows render (skeleton briefly) and the last rows show real names.

User story: As an admin viewing a cmdlet, I want to see other verbs for the same noun so that I can jump from Get-Mailbox to Set-Mailbox.
Expected behaviour: related resolves the key (see find), then collects other rows in the same source with an identical noun, excluding the row itself, stopping at 30 rows taken in index order, then sorts them by verb with localeCompare (search.worker.ts:206-216). Names with no hyphen (empty noun) or unknown keys return []. Duplicated names in other modules with the same noun are included (only the row index is excluded).
How to test: Open Get-Mailbox in Exchange; the related list shows Set-Mailbox, New-Mailbox, Remove-Mailbox etc., alphabetical by verb, never Get-Mailbox itself, and at most 30 entries.

Feature: Find by link key, including legacy, unqualified and duplicate names
User story: As an admin opening a shared link, I want it to resolve to the right cmdlet even if the link is old, differs in case, or the name exists in several modules so that bookmarks keep working.
Expected behaviour: Row keys are 'source:name', qualified as 'source:name@module' only when the name repeats within the source (search.worker.ts:16,32,52). parseKey splits on ':' and '@' (search.worker.ts:33-37). refOfKey finds the source by id (unknown source -> null), compares names case-insensitively, returns the row whose module matches exactly when a module is given, otherwise the first row with that name; an unqualified key or a module that no longer exists falls back to the first same-name row; no name match -> null (search.worker.ts:188-204). find returns that Row or null (search.worker.ts:222-225), and Row.dup tells the UI to show the module (types.ts:230).
How to test: Open a deep link with key 'exchange:get-mailbox' (lower case) and confirm Get-Mailbox opens. For a duplicated name (e.g. an Entra cmdlet in v1.0 and beta), open 'entra:<Name>' without @module and confirm the first one opens; open 'entra:<Name>@<beta module>' and confirm the beta row opens; open 'entra:<Name>@NoSuchModule' and confirm fallback to the first. Open 'nosuch:Get-X' and confirm nothing is selected.

Feature: Search timing shown in result count
User story: As an admin, I want to see how many results matched and how long the search took so that I trust the results are current.
Expected behaviour: The worker measures elapsed time with performance.now() per search (search.worker.ts:146,165). The count label shows formatted count with 'result'/'results' pluralisation and, for non-empty queries, '· <1 ms' when under 1 ms else rounded ms (App.tsx:152). Numbers use en-US grouping (sources.ts:8-10).
How to test: Search 'get-mguser'; label reads like '123 results · 4 ms'. Search a query with one match; label reads '1 result · …'.

User story: As an admin, I want a long result list to scroll smoothly so that I can browse thousands of cmdlets without the page bogging down.
Expected behaviour: Rows are fixed 64px tall (ROW_H) and absolutely positioned at top = i*64px inside .results-inner, whose height is refs.length*64px, so the scrollbar reflects the full result count. Only rows from floor(scrollTop/64)-8 to ceil((scrollTop+clientHeight)/64)+8 (OVERSCAN 8) are in the DOM; the window is recomputed on scroll and on resize (ResizeObserver on the scroller), and the visible window's rows are fetched from the worker via client.request('rows'). A stale fetch is ignored if the window changes first. The scroller #results has role=listbox and aria-label 'Search results'.
How to test: Load the site with an empty query (all results). Count `#results .result` elements: far fewer than the total in `.count`. Check `.results-inner` style height == total*64px. Scroll `#results` to the middle: the rendered rows' `top` values move to match the scroll position and the count of DOM rows stays roughly constant. Resize the window taller: more rows are rendered.

User story: As an admin, I want placeholder rows while the index or row data is loading so that I know results are coming.
Expected behaviour: Before the search client exists (server render / first paint) and while results is null, the list shows 12 shimmering skeleton rows (.result.result-skel, aria-hidden) and the scroller has aria-busy=true. Once results arrive, any row in the visible window whose data has not been fetched yet renders as a skeleton at its position until the 'rows' reply fills it in. Skeletons have cursor:default and two bars at 46% and 78% width; the shimmer is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
How to test: Throttle network in devtools and load /. Before the index loads, `#results` (or `.results[aria-busy=true]`) contains 12 `.result-skel` elements. After load, aria-busy is false and `.result-skel` elements disappear (they may flash when quickly scrolling far down).

Feature: Query highlight marks in result names
User story: As an admin, I want the parts of each cmdlet name that match what I typed to be highlighted so that I can see why a row matched.
Expected behaviour: Each query token (query lowercased, split on whitespace, empty removed) is located by its first case-insensitive occurrence in the row name and wrapped in <mark>, preserving the name's original casing. Marks are sorted by position; a token whose match overlaps an earlier mark is skipped; tokens not found in the name add no mark. With an empty query the name renders without marks.
How to test: Type 'get user' into the search box. In the first `.result-name`, `mark` elements contain 'Get' and 'User' (original case). Type 'zzz mguser': only 'MgUser' style match is marked, no empty marks. Clear the box: no `.result-name mark` elements.

Feature: Row content: source dot, description or module fallback
User story: As an admin, I want each result to show its source colour and a one-line description so that I can pick the right cmdlet at a glance.
Expected behaviour: Each row shows a source-coloured dot (row styled with srcStyle(row.source)), the cmdlet name in <code>, a right-aligned meta tag, and below it the description; if the row has no description the module name is shown instead in a fainter .result-module span. Name and description truncate with ellipsis on one line; the meta tag is capped at 40% width with ellipsis.
How to test: Search for any cmdlet; inspect a `.result`: has `.source-dot`, `code.result-name`, `.result-meta`, `p.result-desc`. Find a row with no description (or wait before descriptions arrive) and confirm `p.result-desc .result-module` holds the module name.

Feature: Row tag: duplicate-name module or beta API
User story: As an admin, I want rows to say which module they come from when a name repeats, or flag beta APIs, so that I don't pick the wrong variant.
Expected behaviour: The .result-meta tag shows the row's module when row.dup is true (the name repeats within its source, e.g. Entra v1.0/beta or Teams/Skype). Otherwise it shows the row's extra value only when it equals the source's warn value ('beta' for Graph and Entra); for all other rows the tag is empty.
How to test: Select the Entra source and search a cmdlet name that exists in both v1.0 and beta modules: two rows with the same name show different module names in `.result-meta`. Select Graph and search a beta cmdlet: `.result-meta` reads 'beta'; a v1.0 Graph cmdlet has empty `.result-meta`.

Feature: Hover moves the cursor highlight; click opens
User story: As an admin, I want hovering a row to highlight it and clicking it to open its details so that mouse and keyboard work together.
Expected behaviour: Moving the mouse over a non-active row makes it the keyboard cursor row (.is-active, surface-2 background) without scrolling the list. Clicking a row opens it in the detail pane: it gets .is-open (source-tinted background) and aria-selected=true, the URL gains the open key, and a pulse is emitted from the detail pane. Arrow keys afterwards continue from the hovered row.
How to test: Search 'user'. Hover the 3rd `.result`: it has class `is-active`, the 1st does not. Press ArrowDown in the search box: the 4th row becomes active. Click a row: it gets `is-open` and `aria-selected="true"`, and the detail pane shows that cmdlet.

User story: As an admin, I want to move through results with the arrow keys from the search box so that I never have to reach for the mouse.
Expected behaviour: With focus in the search box, ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the cursor by one row (default prevented so the caret does not move), clamped to the first and last rows; with no results they do nothing. The list scrolls just enough to keep the cursor row visible (minimal scroll, top or bottom aligned). A new search (new results id) resets the cursor to the first row and scrolls to the top; a refresh of the same search (descriptions arriving) keeps the cursor on the same row (following it if reordered) and reveals it.
How to test: Search 'get'. Press ArrowUp: first row stays `.is-active`. Press ArrowDown 20 times: the 21st row is active and visible inside `#results` (scrollTop > 0). Type another character: first row is active again and scrollTop is 0.

Feature: Enter opens the cursor row, including before results arrive
User story: As an admin, I want to type a name and press Enter immediately so that the top match opens even if the search hasn't finished.
Expected behaviour: Enter in the search box (default prevented) records a pending selection for the latest search id (client.latest) while keeping the currently open entry shown. When that search's results are on screen, the cursor row is opened (fetched from the worker if not yet materialised). If those results are empty the pending Enter is dropped and the previously shown entry remains. Typing again or changing filters before results arrive cancels the pending Enter (settle) and keeps what was shown; clicking another row or Escape also supersedes it. Enter replaces a deep-link lookup still in progress. Enter with no list mounted (load error) does nothing.
How to test: Type 'Get-MgUser' and press Enter in the same instant (e.g. page.type then keyboard.press('Enter')): the detail pane opens Get-MgUser and the URL gains its open key. Search 'qqqqzzzz' and press Enter: nothing opens and the empty state remains. Press ArrowDown twice then Enter: the 3rd row opens.

Feature: Escape closes the entry, then clears the query
User story: As an admin, I want Escape to back out step by step so that I can quickly reset without the mouse.
Expected behaviour: Escape in the search box closes the open entry (or a pending deep link) if there is one; otherwise, if the query is non-empty, it clears the query. With nothing open and an empty query it does nothing. On narrow screens closing the entry slides the full-screen detail pane away.
How to test: Search 'user', press Enter to open a row, press Escape: detail closes (Intro visible, `.app` has no data-open, URL loses the open key) and query remains. Press Escape again: search box value is '' and the clear button is replaced by the '/' hint.

Feature: '/' and Ctrl/Cmd+K focus the search box
User story: As an admin, I want a shortcut to jump back to search from anywhere so that I can start a new lookup instantly.
Expected behaviour: A global keydown listener: '/' pressed while not typing in an input/textarea/select, or Ctrl+K / Cmd+K anywhere (even inside inputs), prevents default, focuses the search box and selects its text. Inside the search box, '/' is swallowed only when the box is empty (so it never types a leading slash); with text present '/' types normally.
How to test: Click a row then click the detail pane, press '/': the search input is focused and its text is selected. Focus a filter select and press Ctrl+K: search input gets focus. With the empty search box focused press '/': value stays ''. Type 'a' then '/': value is 'a/'.

User story: As an admin, I want a one-click way to clear my search and a visible hint of the shortcut so that the box is easy to reset and discover.
Expected behaviour: When the query is empty the right side of the search box shows a <kbd>/</kbd> hint (aria-hidden). When the query is non-empty it shows an X button (aria-label 'Clear search') that clears the query and refocuses the input. The native search-cancel button is hidden. The input is autofocused, has aria-label 'Search cmdlets', aria-controls 'results', spellcheck and autocomplete off.
How to test: On load `.searchbox-kbd` is visible and `.searchbox-clear` absent. Type 'user': `.searchbox-clear` appears, `.searchbox-kbd` gone. Click `button[aria-label="Clear search"]`: input value '' and document.activeElement is the input.

User story: As an admin, I want to see how many results matched and how fast so that I know whether to refine my query.
Expected behaviour: The toolbar .count (aria-live=polite) reads 'Loading index…' before results (also on the server-rendered shell), 'Index unavailable' after a load error, otherwise '<N> results' with N formatted with thousands separators and singular 'result' when N is 1. When the results' query is non-empty it appends ' · <ms> ms' (rounded; '<1' when under 1 ms) in a fainter .ms span; with an empty query no timing is shown.
How to test: Load / with no query: `.count` reads e.g. '12,345 results' with no `.ms`. Type 'Get-MgUser': `.count .ms` matches / · (<1|\d+) ms/. Search an exact unique name to get 1 result: label says '1 result'.

User story: As an admin, I want a helpful message when nothing matches so that I know how to broaden my search.
Expected behaviour: With zero results the scroller gets .results-empty, drops role=listbox, and shows: title 'No match for “<q>”<in Source>.' (e.g. ' in Graph' when a single source is selected, nothing for All) or 'Nothing matches these filters.' when the query is empty; a tip to try the noun alone (MgUser instead of Get-MgUser) or fewer words; and, only when a filter is active or the source is not All, a 'Search every source' chip that resets all filters and the source to All (the query is kept).
How to test: Search 'qqqzzz' on All: `.empty-title` = 'No match for “qqqzzz”.' and no `.empty .chip`. Switch to the Graph tab: title ends ' in Graph.' and a 'Search every source' button appears; click it: All tab is pressed (aria-pressed) and query still 'qqqzzz'. Check `#results` has no role attribute.
Code refs: src/app/ResultList.tsx:112-118, src/app/chrome.tsx:171-179, src/app/App.tsx:194, src/app/sources.ts:57, src/app/sources.ts:69, src/styles/global.css:391-396

User story: As an admin, I want a clear error and a reload button if the search index fails to load so that I can recover.
Expected behaviour: When the worker reports a load error, the results pane is replaced by an alert (role=alert): 'The search index didn’t load.', then '<message>. Check your connection, then reload the page.', and a 'Reload' chip that calls location.reload(). The toolbar reads 'Index unavailable'. Keyboard arrow/Enter navigation does nothing because the list is not mounted; pending worker requests never settle.
How to test: Block the shard/index requests (e.g. route /index/* to 404 or go offline after HTML loads) and load /. Expect `[role=alert] .empty-title` 'The search index didn’t load.', `.count` 'Index unavailable'. Click the 'Reload' button: the page reloads.
Code refs: src/app/App.tsx:63-64, src/app/App.tsx:148-149, src/app/App.tsx:186, src/app/chrome.tsx:181-189, src/app/client.ts:19-24, src/app/client.ts:39-43

User story: As an admin, I want to see the available shortcuts so that I can learn the keyboard flow.
Expected behaviour: The Intro in the detail pane (shown when no entry is open) ends with a legend: '/ search, ↑ ↓ move, Enter open, Esc close' rendered with <kbd> elements. The Intro, including this legend, is hidden at widths <= 900px.
How to test: Load / with no open entry: `.intro-keys kbd` count is 5. Resize viewport to 600px wide: `.intro` is display:none.

User story: As an admin on a phone, I want the results to fill the screen and the detail to slide over them so that lookups work on a small display.
Expected behaviour: At <= 900px the work area becomes a single column with 16px gutters, the search input grows to 52px tall with 16px font (avoids iOS zoom), and opening a result slides the detail pane up as a fixed full-screen overlay (data-open on .app); closing (Escape or the back button) slides it down. Result rows keep ellipsis truncation so no horizontal scroll appears.
How to test: Set viewport to 390x844, search 'user', tap a row: `.pane-detail` covers the viewport (visibility visible, transform none). Press Escape: it hides again. Check document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth <= 390.

Feature: Detail header: cmdlet name and source/module tags
User story: As an admin, I want the opened cmdlet's name, source and module shown at the top of the detail pane so that I know exactly which cmdlet and module I am reading.
Expected behaviour:
Opening a row renders
with its source colour applied via srcStyle (inline style). h2#detail-title contains {row.name}. The .tags row always shows span.tag.tag-source holding a .source-dot plus the source's short label (e.g. Graph, Az, Entra, Exchange, MECM), then span.tag with the module name.
How to test: Search for e.g. Get-MgUser, click the result. Assert #detail-title code text equals the cmdlet name; .detail .tags .tag-source text equals the source short name; the second .tag equals the module (e.g. Microsoft.Graph.Users).

User story: As an admin, I want to see a module's own version when it differs from its source's version so that I know which module release the docs describe.
Expected behaviour: A tag 'v{moduleVersion}' with title="Module version" is shown only when row.moduleVersion is non-empty AND differs from the source's version (e.g. Teams 8.1.0 under Exchange, each Az.* module). It is hidden when moduleVersion is '' or equal to the source version.
How to test: Open an Az cmdlet (e.g. Get-AzVM): assert .tags .tag[title='Module version'] exists with text starting 'v'. Open a cmdlet whose module version equals its source's version (or is unknown): assert that tag is absent.

User story: As an admin, I want the cmdlet's verb shown as a tag so that I can see at a glance whether it reads, creates, changes or removes.
Expected behaviour: When row.verb is non-empty a span.tag with the verb (e.g. Get, Set, New) is rendered after the module/version tags; when verb is empty no verb tag is rendered.
How to test: Open Get-MgUser; assert a .tags .tag with text 'Get' exists.

User story: As an admin, I want a category tag only when it adds information beyond the module name so that the header is not cluttered with repeats.
Expected behaviour: A category tag is shown only when row.category is non-empty, is not equal to row.module, and row.module does not end with '.' + category (e.g. category 'Groups' is hidden for module Microsoft.Graph.Groups).
How to test: Open a Graph cmdlet in Microsoft.Graph.Groups (e.g. Get-MgGroup) and assert no .tag with text 'Groups'. Open a cmdlet whose category differs from its module and assert the category tag is present.

User story: As an admin, I want beta API cmdlets visibly flagged so that I do not accidentally use a beta endpoint in production.
Expected behaviour: When row.extra is non-empty a tag with the extra value (API version for Graph/Entra, site role for MECM) is shown. If the value equals the source's extra.warn ("beta" for Graph and Entra) the tag also has class tag-warn (warning colour). Other extra values (e.g. v1.0) render as a plain tag.
How to test: Open a Graph beta cmdlet (e.g. Get-MgBetaUser): assert .tags .tag.tag-warn with text 'beta'. Open a v1.0 Graph cmdlet: assert the extra tag lacks tag-warn.

User story: As an admin, I want to see how many permissions a cmdlet needs from the header so that I know whether there is a permissions section to review.
Expected behaviour: When row.perms > 0 a tag reads 'N permissions', singular '1 permission' when N is 1. No tag when perms is 0.
How to test: Open a Graph cmdlet with documented permissions; assert a .tag matching /^\d+ permissions?$/ and that its count equals the number of li in ul.perms. Open an Az cmdlet: assert no such tag.

User story: As an admin, I want a one-click link to the official Microsoft Learn page so that I can read the full upstream documentation.
Expected behaviour: a.btn 'Microsoft Learn' with an external-link icon has href https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/{module lowercased}/{name lowercased}, target=_blank, rel=noopener.
How to test: Open Get-MgUser; assert .detail-links a.btn href === 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.graph.users/get-mguser' and target='_blank'.

User story: As an admin, I want to copy the cmdlet name with one click so that I can paste it straight into my shell.
Expected behaviour: An icon button (aria-label/title 'Copy name') next to the title writes row.name to the clipboard. On success the icon switches to a check, the button gets class is-done and aria-label 'Copied' for 1400 ms, then reverts. If the clipboard write rejects (blocked), nothing changes and no error is shown.
How to test: Grant clipboard permission, click #detail-title button[title='Copy name']; assert navigator.clipboard.readText() equals the name and the button has class is-done / aria-label 'Copied', then after ~1.5s aria-label returns to 'Copy name'.

User story: As an admin, I want to copy a direct link to this cmdlet so that I can share it with a colleague and it opens the same entry.
Expected behaviour: A 'Copy link' text button (link icon) copies entryUrl(row.key): origin + pathname with only ?c=<key> (no query or filters). On success its label becomes 'Copied' with a check icon for 1400 ms. Opening that URL opens the same entry (deep link resolved via the worker 'find').
How to test: Open an entry, click .detail-links button containing 'Copy link'; read clipboard, assert it matches /\?c=/ and the button text is 'Copied'. Navigate to the copied URL and assert #detail-title shows the same name.

Feature: Loading skeleton while module file loads
User story: As an admin, I want a visible loading state while details are fetched so that I know the pane is working.
Expected behaviour: While the module file is being fetched, a div.detail-skel with aria-busy="true" and aria-label="Loading details" containing four shimmering span bars is shown under the header (header tags/links render immediately from the row).
How to test: Throttle network, open an uncached cmdlet; assert .detail-skel[aria-busy='true'] is present, then disappears when content loads.

User story: As an admin, I want a clear error if the details cannot be loaded so that I know to retry instead of seeing a blank pane.
Expected behaviour: If the module file fetch fails (non-2xx gives 'HTTP <status> for <path>'; network error) or the file has no record for the row's name (index and file from different deploys: 'no record for <name>'), a p.notice.notice-error role=alert reads 'Couldn’t load details (<message>). Check your connection and pick the cmdlet again.' A failed fetch is evicted from the module cache so reopening the cmdlet retries.
How to test: Block requests to /a/*/data/* (route abort), open a cmdlet; assert [role=alert].notice-error contains 'Couldn’t load details'. Unblock, open another row then the same one again; assert details render.

User story: As an admin, I want cmdlets from a module I've already opened to show instantly so that browsing related cmdlets is fast.
Expected behaviour: loadModule caches the fetch promise per source/file key; opening another cmdlet in the same module file reuses it with no new network request. Rejected promises are removed from the cache.
How to test: Open one cmdlet, then another in the same module (e.g. via the Same noun list); assert no second request to the same /a/<build>/data/<source>/<file> URL in the network log.

User story: As an admin, I want the cmdlet's description shown first so that I can confirm it does what I need.
Expected behaviour: When the cmdlet has a description it is rendered as p.detail-desc above the syntax; nothing is rendered when empty.
How to test: Open a cmdlet with a synopsis; assert .detail-desc is present with non-empty text.

Feature: Syntax parameter sets with highlighting and copy
User story: As an admin, I want each parameter set's syntax shown, highlighted and copyable so that I can see valid argument combinations and paste a template.
Expected behaviour: Syntax text is split into parameter sets on blank lines; each non-empty set renders as div.code.code-syntax with a pre/code body and a 'Copy code' small icon button that copies the set's groups joined with single spaces (whitespace normalised). Heading is 'Syntax', with ' · N parameter sets' note when there is more than one set. Each top-level group (e.g. '-Name <T>', '[-Opt <T>]', '[-Switch]') is a span.sg that does not wrap internally, so lines break only between parameters; a bare <Type> joins the preceding group; brackets/angles are respected including malformed '[-Status <StatusEnum]'. Tokens are highlighted as t-cmd, t-param, t-type, etc. The section is omitted when there is no syntax.
How to test: Open a cmdlet with multiple parameter sets (e.g. Get-MgUser); assert h3 text contains 'parameter sets' and count of .code-syntax equals N; assert .code-syntax .sg elements exist and first contains span.t-cmd; click its 'Copy code' button and assert clipboard is a single-spaced line starting with the cmdlet name.

User story: As an admin, I want a table of parameters with types and required/positional markers so that I know what I must supply.
Expected behaviour: Parameters parsed from all syntax sets are deduplicated by name, shown in table.params with columns Name (code.t-param '-Name' plus optional p.param-desc), Type (code.t-type; 'Switch' when no type), and a visually-hidden 'Required' column. A parameter is Required (span.tag.tag-req) only if every set requires it; otherwise a '[-Name] <T>' parameter shows a 'Positional' tag; otherwise empty. Required parameters are sorted first. If a name's first occurrence was a switch, a later typed occurrence supplies its type. The section is omitted when no visible parameters.
How to test: Open a cmdlet with a mandatory parameter (e.g. New-MgUser or Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName); assert table.params rows exist, rows with .tag-req appear before those without, and a switch parameter shows type 'Switch'.

Feature: Hide pipeline/proxy common parameters behind a toggle
User story: As an admin, I want boilerplate pipeline and proxy parameters hidden by default so that the table shows the parameters that matter.
Expected behaviour: Parameters named Break, Headers, HttpPipelineAppend, HttpPipelinePrepend, Proxy, ProxyCredential, ProxyUseDefaultCredentials, ResponseHeadersVariable, WhatIf, Confirm, DefaultProfile are hidden initially and sorted last. A button.link-btn 'Show N pipeline and proxy parameters' (N = hidden count) appears when any are hidden; clicking it reveals them and the button disappears. State resets when a different entry opens.
How to test: Open a Graph cmdlet; assert no row with '-HttpPipelineAppend', click button.link-btn matching /Show \d+ pipeline and proxy parameters/, assert the row appears and the button is gone.

User story: As an admin using ConfigMgr cmdlets, I want parameter descriptions from the docs so that I understand each parameter without leaving the page.
Expected behaviour: When the cmdlet file has documented parameters (MECM pipeline), the table lists exactly those in documented order with their required flag and description (p.param-desc); type comes from the documentation, else from parsed syntax, else ''; positional comes from the syntax. Without documented parameters the parsed list is used unchanged.
How to test: Open an MECM cmdlet (e.g. Get-CMDevice); assert table.params rows contain p.param-desc text.

User story: As an admin, I want the required permissions listed and copyable so that I can grant consent or request scopes quickly.
Expected behaviour: When the cmdlet has permissions, a 'Permissions' section shows each as li code in ul.perms, and a small 'Copy all permissions' icon button copies them joined with ', '. Omitted when there are none.
How to test: Open a Graph cmdlet with permissions; assert ul.perms li count > 0; click button[title='Copy all permissions'] and assert clipboard equals li texts joined by ', '.

Feature: Examples with tokenised highlighting and copy
User story: As an admin, I want highlighted, copyable examples so that I can adapt a working command quickly.
Expected behaviour: The Examples section always renders. Each example is div.code with tokenised spans: t-com (# comments), t-str (double/single quoted strings incl. backtick escapes and '' doubling), t-var ($x, ${...}, $env:X), t-cmd (Verb-Noun), t-param (-Name not preceded by word char/hyphen), t-type (<T> or [Type] before a value), t-num, t-op (| { } ( ) = ; @ ,); other text is plain. Each has a 'Copy code' button copying the raw example text verbatim (newlines kept). With no examples it shows p.h-sub 'The docs have no example for this cmdlet. Start from the syntax above.'
How to test: Open a cmdlet with examples; assert .code:not(.code-syntax) pre contains span.t-cmd and span.t-var; click its Copy code button and compare clipboard with pre textContent. Open a cmdlet without examples and assert the 'The docs have no example' text.

User story: As an admin, I want to jump to other cmdlets with the same noun so that I can find the Set/Remove counterpart of the Get I just read.
Expected behaviour: After the worker answers 'related', a section 'Same noun · {noun}' (text after the first '-' in the name) lists up to 30 other cmdlets in the same source with the same noun (case-insensitive), excluding the current one, sorted by verb. Each is a button with code name; when the name repeats in its source (dup) it adds ' · {module}'. Clicking opens that entry. Section omitted when none; related list is not carried over from the previous entry.
How to test: Open Get-MgUser; assert section h3 'Same noun · MgUser' with ul.related buttons (e.g. New-MgUser, Update-MgUser) sorted by verb; click one and assert #detail-title changes to it.

User story: As an admin on a phone, I want the detail to open full screen with a back button so that I can read it and return to my results.
Expected behaviour: At widths <=900px the detail pane is fixed full-screen, sliding up (transform 260ms) when an entry is open; .detail-back (ArrowLeft, aria-label 'Back to results') is visible, and clicking it closes the entry (clears ?c from URL, pane slides away). On wider screens the back button is hidden (display:none). Escape in the search box also closes an open entry. Syntax blocks fade out at the right edge and the required column may wrap.
How to test: Set viewport 390x844, open a result; assert .pane-detail visible and button[aria-label='Back to results'] visible; click it and assert URL lacks c= and pane is hidden. At 1280px width assert the back button is not visible.

Feature: Scroll reset and fresh state per entry
User story: As an admin, I want each new cmdlet to open at the top with fresh content so that I don't land mid-page or see stale data from the previous cmdlet.
Expected behaviour: Detail is keyed by row.key, so opening a different entry remounts it (loading skeleton, collapsed common parameters, empty related list). A layout effect sets the detail pane's scrollTop to 0 whenever the open key changes. Stale async replies for a previous entry are ignored (live flags).
How to test: Open a long cmdlet, scroll .pane-detail down, click a Same noun related button; assert .pane-detail scrollTop === 0 and the new name in #detail-title.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
User story: As an admin, I want a row of source tabs (All, Graph, Az, Entra, Exchange, MECM) each showing its cmdlet count so that I can see at a glance how big each docs set is and narrow my search to one.
Expected behaviour: The band renders a <nav class="sources" aria-label="Source"> with an 'All' tab first (count = TOTAL from sources.generated.json, e.g. 40,931) followed by one tab per SOURCES entry in generated order, labelled with its `short` name and its build-time `count` formatted en-US with thousands separators (e.g. 'Graph 27,327'). Counts are static per build and do not change with the query or filters. Exactly one tab has class 'is-on' and aria-pressed="true": the one matching filters.source. Each tab is tinted via the --src CSS variable set to its source colour (All uses #b9c3d6) and shows a coloured dot.
How to test: Load /. Assert `.sources .source` count = SOURCES.length+1; first tab text contains 'All' and formatCount(total); `.source.is-on` has text 'All' and aria-pressed=true; each other tab's `.source-n` equals formatCount(source.count). Load /?s=az and assert the Az tab is the only `.is-on`.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Switching source scopes search, placeholder and tint
User story: As an admin, I want clicking a source tab to restrict results to that source and retint the page so that I know which docs set I am searching.
Expected behaviour: Clicking a tab calls setSource(id): filters.source becomes that id and a new search runs over only that source's shards (worker filters scope by scopeOf(source).sources). The search input placeholder changes to 'Search <count> <short> cmdlets' (e.g. 'Search 8,819 Az cmdlets'), or 'Search 40,931 cmdlets' for All. The .app root's --src style changes to the source colour. The URL gets s=<id> (s is omitted for All). The result count label in the toolbar reflects the new scope.
How to test: Load /. Click `.source:has-text("Az")`; assert URL param s=az, input placeholder 'Search 8,819 Az cmdlets', every `.result` belongs to Az (names start with Az-style prefixes). Click `.source:has-text("All")`; assert no s param and placeholder 'Search 40,931 cmdlets'.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Which filters survive a source switch
User story: As an admin, I want my verb and has-examples filters to carry over when I change source, while source-specific filters reset, so that I can compare e.g. all Remove- cmdlets across sources without stale per-source filters.
Expected behaviour: setSource builds filters from EMPTY_FILTERS with the new source plus the previous verb and examples only. module, category (cat) and extra (ver) are cleared. The search query q is untouched. Example: from /?s=graph&verb=Remove&ver=beta clicking Az yields s=az&verb=Remove with no ver, and results are Remove-Az* cmdlets.
How to test: Go to /?s=graph&verb=Remove&ver=beta&cat=X&ex=1&q=user. Click `.source:has-text("Az")`. Assert URL has s=az, verb=Remove, ex=1, q=user and no ver/cat/module; first `.result .result-name` starts with 'Remove-Az'.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Selected source tab stays visible on narrow screens
User story: As an admin on a phone, I want the source tab strip to scroll sideways and keep the selected tab in view so that I can reach every source without the page scrolling horizontally.
Expected behaviour: At viewport width <=900px the .sources strip stops wrapping (flex-wrap: nowrap), scrolls horizontally with a hidden scrollbar, bleeds to the 16px gutters and fades out its right 48px via mask-image; tabs do not shrink. When a tab becomes selected (including on load from ?s=), it calls scrollIntoView({block:'nearest', inline:'nearest'}) so it is brought into view. Above 900px tabs wrap.
How to test: Set viewport 375x800, load /?s=mecm. Assert `.sources` computed flex-wrap is nowrap and scrollLeft > 0 so the MECM tab's bounding rect is within the strip; document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Filters toggle chip with active-filter count
User story: As an admin, I want a Filters chip that opens the filter bar and shows how many filters are narrowing results so that I notice when results are filtered even with the bar closed.
Expected behaviour: The toolbar has a button.chip with aria-controls="filters" and aria-expanded reflecting whether the bar is shown. The filter bar is hidden by default on every load (showFilters is not stored in the URL); clicking the chip toggles it. The chip shows a `.chip-n` badge with activeFilters(filters): the number of non-source filters (verb, module, category, extra, examples) differing from empty; no badge when 0. The source is not counted. The chip has class 'is-on' when the bar is open OR any filter is active.
How to test: Load /?s=graph&verb=Get&ex=1. Assert `button[aria-controls=filters]` aria-expanded=false, `.chip-n` text '2', class contains is-on, `#filters` absent. Click it: `#filters` present, aria-expanded=true. Load /?s=graph: no `.chip-n`.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
User story: As an admin, I want the filter dropdowns to offer only values that exist in the current scope so that I can narrow by verb, module, category or the source's special facet without guessing.
Expected behaviour: Facets come from the worker for the current scope, each sorted with localeCompare and de-duplicated with empties removed. Verb select shows when there is >=1 verb. Module select shows only when >1 module, and modules are only computed for a single source (empty for All, so no Module select under All). Category select shows when >1 category (computed for All too). The extra select shows only when the scope has an extraLabel (single source with `extra` metadata) and >1 extra value; it is labelled with that label: 'API' for Graph and Entra, 'Site role' for MECM; Az and Exchange have none. Each select has a first option 'Any' (value ''); choosing a value sets the filter and reruns the search. Facets reflect the whole scope, not the current query. Before results arrive, facets are empty (only checkbox and Reset show).
How to test: Load /, open filters: assert labels include 'Verb' and not 'Module' or 'API'. Click Graph tab: labels include 'Verb','Module' and 'API'; API select options include 'Any' and 'beta'. Click Az: no 'API' label. Click MECM: a 'Site role' select. Choose Verb 'Get' and assert URL verb=Get and all results start with 'Get-'.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
User story: As an admin, I want to show only cmdlets whose docs include examples so that I can copy a working command quickly.
Expected behaviour: The filter bar has a 'Has examples' checkbox bound to filters.examples. Checking it restricts results to rows whose shard `e` flag is set and writes ex=1 to the URL; unchecking removes ex. Only the literal value ex=1 reads as true from the URL (ex=true or ex=0 read as false). It counts toward the Filters chip number and survives source switches.
How to test: Open /?s=graph, open filters, check `.filters input[type=checkbox]`; assert URL ex=1 and the count decreases. Load /?ex=true and assert checkbox unchecked and no ex in rewritten URL.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
User story: As an admin, I want a Reset button in the filter bar that clears every filter but keeps my chosen source so that I can start narrowing again without losing scope.
Expected behaviour: Clicking `.filters .link-btn` (text 'Reset') sets filters to EMPTY_FILTERS with source preserved: verb, module, cat, ver and ex removed. The query q is not cleared. E.g. /?s=graph&verb=Get&ex=1 becomes ?s=graph.
How to test: Go to /?s=graph&verb=Get&ex=1, click `button[aria-controls=filters]`, then `.filters .link-btn`; wait for location.search === '?s=graph'.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: URL round trip of search state
User story: As an admin, I want the address bar to always reflect my query, source, filters and open entry so that I can bookmark, reload or share exactly what I see.
Expected behaviour: State is read once on mount from location.search: q, s (source), verb, module, cat (category), ver (extra), ex (examples), c (open entry). On every change of q, filters or open key, writeUrl rebuilds the query string in the fixed order q, s, verb, module, cat, ver, ex, c, omitting empty values, s=all and ex when false; the bare pathname when nothing is set. It uses history.replaceState (no new history entries, Back leaves the page) and skips the call when the URL is already identical. Values are URL-encoded by URLSearchParams. Typing in the box updates q on each input.
How to test: Load /?ex=1&verb=Get&s=graph&q=user; assert after mount location.search === '?q=user&s=graph&verb=Get&ex=1' and history.length unchanged after typing more. Reload and assert the input value is 'user', Graph tab is on, filters restored (open filters: verb select 'Get', checkbox checked).

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Unknown or stale source id falls back to All
User story: As an admin following an old link with a source that no longer exists, I want the page to still work by searching every source.
Expected behaviour: parseScope maps a missing or unknown s value (e.g. s=intune or s=ALL) to 'all'. The All tab is selected, all sources are searched, and the s parameter is dropped from the URL on the first write. Other filters in the link are kept.
How to test: Load /?s=bogus&q=user. Assert `.source.is-on` is 'All', and location.search === '?q=user'.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Per-source filters in an All-scope URL
User story: As an admin opening a hand-edited link like /?module=X with no source, I want the filter to still apply and be counted so that results are consistent with the link.
Expected behaviour: module and ver values are applied by the worker regardless of scope (passes() checks every set filter), but under All the Module and extra selects are not rendered because those facets are empty for All. The Filters chip still counts them, and Reset clears them. Unknown verb/cat values simply produce zero matches.
How to test: Load /?module=Microsoft.Graph.Users. Assert `.chip-n` text '1', open filters and assert no 'Module' select, results all come from that module; click Reset and assert URL has no module.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Deep link to an entry (qualified key)
User story: As an admin, I want a link with c=<source>:<name>@<module> to open that exact cmdlet so that shared links land on the right page even when a name repeats in a source.
Expected behaviour: On load with c set, the selection is {link} and the c value stays in the URL while the worker 'find' request runs (a reload mid-lookup still opens it). The worker parses key as source:name@module, matches the name case-insensitively within that source, and returns the row with that module. On reply the detail pane opens that row; the URL's c is replaced with the row's canonical key (`source:name`, plus `@module` only when the name repeats in that source). Opening the entry does not change q or filters (e.g. /?s=entra&q=Connect-Entra&c=entra:Connect-Entra keeps all three).
How to test: Load /?c=exchange:Get-CsExternalAccessPolicy@MicrosoftTeams; assert the detail pane shows Get-CsExternalAccessPolicy from MicrosoftTeams and c is unchanged. Load /?c=graph:get-mguser (lowercase) and assert c is rewritten to 'graph:Get-MgUser'.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Legacy/unqualified deep links adopt the canonical key
User story: As an admin following an older link that omits the module or names a module that no longer applies, I want it to still open the cmdlet so that old bookmarks keep working.
Expected behaviour: If the key has no @module, or no row with that module exists, refOfKey falls back to the first row in that source with the same name (case-insensitive). The entry opens and the URL's c is updated to that row's canonical key (which gains @module if the name is duplicated in the source).
How to test: Load /?c=exchange:Get-CsExternalAccessPolicy (name duplicated in Exchange); assert the detail opens and c becomes 'exchange:Get-CsExternalAccessPolicy@<module>'. Load /?c=mecm:Invoke-CMClientAction@OldModule; assert it opens and c becomes 'mecm:Invoke-CMClientAction'.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
User story: As an admin following a broken entry link, I want the page to fall back to the normal search view instead of an error.
Expected behaviour: If the source in c is unknown or no row has that name, 'find' returns null; the selection becomes null, the detail pane shows the Intro (wide screens), and c is removed from the URL. Other parameters remain. If the user opens another entry or presses Enter before the lookup returns, the stale lookup result is ignored (live flag).
How to test: Load /?q=user&c=graph:No-SuchCmdlet; wait for results; assert location.search === '?q=user' and `.intro` is visible (viewport >900px). Load /?c=nosource:Get-X and assert c removed.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Closing an entry removes it from the URL
User story: As an admin, I want closing the open cmdlet to clear it from the link so that the URL matches what I see.
Expected behaviour: Escape in the search box closes an open entry (or pending deep link) first; the c parameter is removed while q and filters stay. If nothing is open, Escape clears the query instead (removing q).
How to test: Load /?q=user&c=graph:Get-MgUser; focus input; press Escape; assert location.search === '?q=user'. Press Escape again; assert location.search === ''.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
User story: As an admin, I want clicking the PSIndex wordmark to reset everything so that I can start a fresh lookup in one click.
Expected behaviour: The wordmark is <a class="wordmark" href="/" aria-label="PSIndex home">. A normal click is intercepted (preventDefault, no page reload) and clears q, resets filters to EMPTY_FILTERS (source All, no filters) and closes any open entry; the URL becomes the bare pathname. Because href is '/', open-in-new-tab still loads the home page. The Filters bar open/closed state is not changed.
How to test: Load /?q=user&s=graph&verb=Get&c=graph:Get-MgUser. Click `a.wordmark`. Assert location.search === '', input value '', All tab `.is-on`, no detail open, and performance navigation count unchanged (no reload).

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
User story: As an admin new to the site, I want one-click sample searches per source so that I can see how the index works.
Expected behaviour: When no entry is open, the detail pane shows the Intro with a list 'Example searches' containing one button per source (tinted by source colour) showing its sample: Get-MgUser (Graph), Get-AzVM (Az), Get-EntraGroupMember (Entra), Set-Mailbox (Exchange), Invoke-CMClientAction (MECM). Clicking one calls setSource(that source) (keeping verb and has-examples, dropping module/cat/ver), sets q to the sample, and focuses the search input. The URL becomes ?q=<sample>&s=<id>[&verb…&ex=1].
How to test: At 1280px width load /. Click `.intro-samples button:has-text("Get-AzVM")`. Assert input value 'Get-AzVM', document.activeElement is the search input, URL q=Get-AzVM&s=az, Az tab on.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Intro source list with counts and versions
User story: As an admin, I want the intro to list each docs set with its cmdlet count and module version so that I know how current the index is.
Expected behaviour: The Intro lede reads '<TOTAL> cmdlets from <N> Microsoft docs sets, searched in your browser…'. A <dl class="intro-sources"> has one row per source: dt with coloured dot and full label (e.g. 'Microsoft Graph', 'Configuration Manager') and dd with formatted count and ' · v<version>' (e.g. '27,327 · v2.41.2'). A keyboard hint line shows '/ search, ↑↓ move, Enter open, Esc close'. The whole Intro is hidden (display:none) at <=900px width, and replaced by the Detail when an entry is open. The server-rendered Shell also shows the Intro (inert) before the app mounts.
How to test: At 1280px load /; assert `.intro-sources > div` count = 5 and text of the Graph row contains 'Microsoft Graph' and '27,327 · v2.41.2'. Resize to 375px; assert `.intro` not visible.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
User story: As an admin, I want the header to state which products are covered so that I know whether my cmdlet is in scope.
Expected behaviour: The band shows a tagline 'PowerShell cmdlets for Graph, Az, Entra, Exchange, and MECM. One index.' built with Intl.ListFormat over SOURCES short names. It is hidden at viewport width <=1100px.
How to test: At 1280px load /; assert `.tagline` text equals 'PowerShell cmdlets for Graph, Az, Entra, Exchange, and MECM. One index.'. At 1000px assert it is not visible.

User story: As an admin, I want the page frame to appear immediately while the search session starts so that I see where to type before the index loads.
Expected behaviour: The SSR/first-paint render is <Shell/> (App returns Shell until a mount effect flips `mounted`). Shell renders Frame with inert=true, so the root .app div carries aria-busy="true"; the band shows the All tab selected, empty query, placeholder `Search <TOTAL> cmdlets`; the toolbar count reads "Loading index…" with a 0-count Filters chip; the results pane shows ResultsSkeleton shimmer rows and the detail pane shows the Intro. All handlers are no-ops (INERT_BAND). Once mounted in the browser, Search replaces Shell and aria-busy is removed (attribute omitted when inert is false).
How to test: curl the built dist/index.html (or view-source) and assert `.app[aria-busy="true"]`, `.count` text "Loading index…", `.result-skel` elements and `.intro` present. In a browser after load, assert `document.querySelector('.app').hasAttribute('aria-busy') === false`.

Feature: Page title, description, OG and theme-color meta
User story: As an admin, I want a descriptive tab title and link preview so that I can find and share the tool.
Expected behaviour: <title> is "PSIndex — PowerShell cmdlet search for Microsoft 365 and Azure"; meta description and og:description are "Search <formatted TOTAL> <SOURCE_LABELS> cmdlets in one place."; og:title is "PSIndex"; lang=en; viewport width=device-width; meta color-scheme "dark light"; theme-color #090c13 for prefers-color-scheme dark and #eef0f5 for light (media-based only, not following the manual override); favicon /favicon.svg.
How to test: Build, then grep dist/index.html for the <title>, meta[name=description], meta[property^=og:], two meta[name=theme-color] with media attributes, and link[rel=icon][href="/favicon.svg"]. Check the description count matches the sum of source counts.

User story: As an admin with JavaScript disabled, I want to be told why search does not work so that I know to enable it.
Expected behaviour: A <noscript> paragraph with 24px padding reads "PSIndex searches in your browser and needs JavaScript." It appears below the (inert) SSR shell when scripts are disabled.
How to test: Open the built site with JavaScript disabled (e.g. Playwright javaScriptEnabled:false) and assert the text "PSIndex searches in your browser and needs JavaScript." is visible.

User story: As an admin who chose a theme, I want it applied before the page paints so that I do not see a flash of the wrong theme.
Expected behaviour: An inline head script reads localStorage['psindex-theme'] and, if set, writes it to <html data-theme> before body render; errors (blocked storage) are swallowed. CSS tokens for light apply under :root[data-theme='light'] and for dark override under :root:not([data-theme='dark']) in a light OS; the body background uses var(--bg).
How to test: In a browser: localStorage.setItem('psindex-theme','light'); reload; assert document.documentElement.dataset.theme==='light' and getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor is rgb(238,240,245) even with emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark.

User story: As an admin, I want a button to switch between light and dark so that the page suits my surroundings, and have it remembered.
Expected behaviour: The band button aria-label "Toggle light or dark theme" flips the on-screen theme (stored override, else OS) to the opposite, sets <html data-theme> to it and stores it in localStorage 'psindex-theme' (storage failures ignored; the theme still changes for the session). The icon shows a sun in dark theme and a moon in light theme, including when no data-theme is set (follows prefers-color-scheme). Only 'light'/'dark' stored values are honoured by the hook; other values are treated as no override.
How to test: Click button[aria-label="Toggle light or dark theme"]; assert html[data-theme] flips and localStorage.getItem('psindex-theme') equals it; assert .i-sun visible when dark and .i-moon visible when light; reload and assert the theme persists.

Feature: Follow the OS theme until overridden
User story: As an admin who has not picked a theme, I want the page to follow my OS light/dark setting live so that it matches the rest of my desktop.
Expected behaviour: With no stored override, the theme is the prefers-color-scheme value and updates live on OS change (matchMedia change listener) for both CSS tokens and the ASCII field tint. Once the toggle has stored an override, OS changes no longer affect the theme (override ?? os).
How to test: Clear localStorage; in Playwright emulate colorScheme 'dark' then 'light' without reload; assert body background changes and html has no data-theme. Then click the toggle and switch emulation again; assert the theme stays at the chosen value.

Feature: Animated ASCII density field behind the UI
User story: As an admin, I want a subtle animated background so that the page feels alive without getting in the way.
Expected behaviour: A fixed full-viewport <canvas class="field" aria-hidden="true"> with pointer-events:none sits under the band and work area (z-index 0 vs 1). It draws a flowing contour field of glyphs from ' .·:-=+*%#@' (denser cells occasionally show PowerShell sigils $|{}<>;), at ~30 fps, strongest across the top (~420px, or 520px under 640px wide) and fading to a quiet floor below. Moving the pointer brightens cells within 160px. Canvas resolution is capped at 2x DPR and resizes with the window; under 640px wide cells are 12px instead of 14px.
How to test: Load the site, assert canvas.field exists with aria-hidden=true and computed pointer-events none and position fixed; screenshot twice ~500ms apart and assert pixels differ; resize window and assert canvas.style.width equals innerWidth px.

Feature: Field tinted by selected source and theme
User story: As an admin, I want the background colour to reflect the source I am searching so that I always know which docs set is in scope.
Expected behaviour: The field colour is the current scope's colour (All = #b9c3d6, each source its own colour). In light theme glyphs are darkened (RGB x0.62) with opacity factor 0.85; in dark theme the raw colour with 0.78. Switching source or theme re-bakes the glyph atlas (no-op if the tone is unchanged) and, under reduced motion, redraws immediately. The same --src hue tints the .app (wordmark 'PS', search caret and focus ring, active tab).
How to test: Click a source tab; sample canvas pixel colours (or check .app style --src) and assert they match that source's colour; toggle theme and assert the field glyphs become darker in light theme.

Feature: Ripple on typing and on opening an entry
User story: As an admin, I want visual feedback in the background as I type and open results so that each step of a lookup feels responsive.
Expected behaviour: Each input event sends a ripple (amp 1) from the point just after the typed text in the search box (clamped to 24px before the input's right edge, vertically centred). Opening an entry sends a ripple (amp 0.7) from 40px inside the detail pane's top-left, only if the pane has a width. Ripples expand at 520px/s, fade over 2.2s, and at most 8 are kept (oldest dropped).
How to test: Type characters into input[aria-label="Search cmdlets"] and take rapid canvas screenshots, asserting a brightening ring near the caret; click a result and assert a ring originates near the detail pane top-left.
