User story: As an admin, I want the background to step back behind the logo, tagline and buttons so that they stay readable.
Expected behaviour: Elements marked data-quiet (wordmark, tagline, band actions) are measured on resize and after web fonts load; cells within qpad (18px, or 6px under 640px wide) of them are attenuated to as low as 8% strength, ramping back to full at the edge of the pad.
How to test: Screenshot the canvas region behind .wordmark and .band-actions and compare glyph density with an equal area away from them; assert near-empty around the elements.

Feature: Field pauses when tab hidden and cleans up
User story: As an admin with many tabs open, I want the animation to stop when the tab is hidden so that it does not waste CPU or battery.
Expected behaviour: On visibilitychange to hidden the requestAnimationFrame loop stops; when visible again it restarts (or, under reduced motion, draws one static frame). On unmount, dispose() stops drawing and aborts all window/document/media listeners via an AbortController.
How to test: In Playwright, spy on requestAnimationFrame, dispatch visibilitychange with document.hidden=true (or switch tabs) and assert no further frames are scheduled; return to the tab and assert frames resume.

Feature: Reduced motion: static field and no transitions
User story: As an admin who prefers reduced motion, I want the background and UI to stop animating so that the page is comfortable to use.
Expected behaviour: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the field draws a single static frame (time frozen at 0 + seed) and never starts the rAF loop; switching the preference live stops and redraws, or restarts the animation when turned off. Globally, all CSS animations/transitions are shortened to 0.01ms (skeleton shimmer, detail slide-in, hover fades).
How to test: Emulate reducedMotion 'reduce'; take two canvas screenshots 1s apart and assert identical; assert getComputedStyle(.pane-detail).transitionDuration is ~0.01ms. Toggle emulation to 'no-preference' and assert the canvas animates again.

User story: As an admin on a desktop, I want results and details side by side with independent scrolling so that I can browse and read at once.
Expected behaviour: The .app grid fills 100dvh (max width 1560px, centred) with the band on top and a work area below; over 900px wide, the work area has columns minmax(340px,5fr) and minmax(0,7fr) with 14px gap. Results and detail panes scroll independently; opening a new entry resets the detail pane's scrollTop to 0. Between 900 and 1100px the tagline is hidden.
How to test: At 1400x900 viewport, assert .pane-results and .pane-detail are side by side (different left offsets, same top); scroll detail, open another result, assert .pane-detail.scrollTop===0. At 1000px width assert .tagline is display:none.

Feature: Horizontally scrolling source tab strip on narrow screens
User story: As an admin on a narrow screen, I want the source tabs in a single swipeable row that keeps my selection visible so that the header stays compact.
Expected behaviour: At <=900px .sources does not wrap, scrolls horizontally with hidden scrollbar, bleeds to the screen edges (-16px margins) and fades out over its last 48px via a mask. Whenever a tab becomes selected it is scrolled into view (scrollIntoView block/inline 'nearest'), e.g. when a deep link or Intro sample selects a source off-screen. Band padding becomes 30px 16px 14px and the search input is 52px high with a 16px font (avoids iOS zoom).
How to test: At 390px width, assert .sources scrollWidth > clientWidth and flex-wrap nowrap; load /?source=<last source id> and assert that tab's bounding rect lies within the .sources viewport; assert input font-size 16px.

User story: As a keyboard-using admin, I want a clear focus indicator so that I can see where I am.
Expected behaviour: :focus-visible draws a 2px outline mixing the current --src hue 80% with white (dark) or black (light), 2px offset, 6px radius. The search box shows a source-coloured border and 4px glow on focus-within instead of an outline; text selection is tinted with the source colour.
How to test: Tab to a source tab button and assert computed outline-style solid, outline-width 2px; focus the search input and assert .searchbox box-shadow is non-none.

User story: As a maintainer, I want the index build to refuse to run when the source lists disagree so that a source added or removed in one place cannot silently be missing from the site or the refresh workflow.
Expected behaviour: Before anything is written, checkRegistries() compares the sorted ids of SOURCES (graph, az, entra, exchange, mecm) with the sorted directory names under data/ and the directories under pipelines/ that contain a source.env. If either list differs, the build throws `Source lists disagree. SOURCES: <ids>; data/: <dirs>; pipelines/*/source.env: <dirs>` and exits 1 (main().catch -> process.exit(1)); public/a/ is not removed because the check runs before rm(OUT). Directories under pipelines/ without source.env (e.g. __pycache__) are ignored; plain files in data/ are ignored.
How to test: Copy the repo to a scratch dir; `mkdir data/foo && npm run index` -> exit code 1 and stderr contains 'Source lists disagree' and 'data/: az,entra,exchange,foo,graph,mecm'. Revert, then `mkdir pipelines/bar && touch pipelines/bar/source.env && npm run index` -> same error naming pipelines list. With a clean tree `npm run index` exits 0.

User story: As a maintainer, I want a malformed data/<source>/manifest.json or descriptions.json to fail the build with a precise message so that a parser change that breaks the shape never ships a broken index.
Expected behaviour: loadRows throws (build exits 1) when: manifest is not an object (`<id> manifest: not an object`); descriptions.json is not an object of strings (`<id> descriptions: not an object of strings`); manifest.d is not an array (`<id> manifest: d is not a list`); manifest.v is missing, non-string or empty (`<id> manifest: v is not a version string`). Per row (parseManifestRow): non-object row; missing/non-string n (`n (name) is not a string`); non-string v or c (`<k> is not a string`); m missing for a source without a fixed module (all but mecm) or empty (`no module`); the row's name appears in no module file (`no module file`); the module matches none of the files holding the name (`module <m> matches none of its files (<files>)`); for sources with an extra facet (graph/entra field a, mecm field r) the field must be a string. Errors are prefixed `<id> manifest, <name>:`. For mecm, a row without m gets module 'ConfigurationManager' and resolves to the single file holding the name.
How to test: In a scratch copy, edit data/az/manifest.json: set "v":"" -> `npm run index` fails with 'az manifest: v is not a version string'. Restore; remove the 'm' key from one az row -> fails with 'az manifest, <name>: m is not a string'. Restore; change one graph row's m to 'Nope' -> 'module Nope matches none of its files'. Restore; delete a graph row's 'a' -> 'a is not a string'.

User story: As a maintainer, I want each data/<source>/modules/*.json file to be checked and normalized so that the detail pane always receives every field in a known shape.
Expected behaviour: For each *.json in modules/ (sorted): fails with `<id>/<file>: cmdlets is not an object` if the file or its cmdlets is not an object; fails with `<id>/<file>: version is not a string` if version is present, non-null and not a string (null/absent -> ''). Each cmdlet must have string syntax and string[] examples; permissions if present must be string[]; parameters if present must be {name,type,required:boolean,description?:string}[]; otherwise `<id>/<file> <name>: ...` error. Output detail: blank/whitespace examples removed, permissions default [], parameters default [] with description defaulting to '', description taken from descriptions.json (or ''). Row flag e = detail has examples, p = permission count, read from the normalized file entry (not from the manifest's e/p).
How to test: In a scratch copy, set one cmdlet's examples to a string in data/az/modules/Az.Compute.json -> `npm run index` fails with 'az/Az.Compute.json <name>: examples is not a list of strings'. Set version to 5 -> 'version is not a string'. With clean data, run `npm run index` and inspect public/a/<build>/data/mecm/*.json: every entry has syntax, examples, permissions, parameters, description keys.

Feature: Columnar shard and description shard output
User story: As a maintainer, I want the build to emit one compact columnar search shard and an aligned description array per source so that the worker can load search data quickly and descriptions later.
Expected behaviour: Rows are sorted by name (localeCompare). Each source writes idx/<id>.json with parallel arrays n, v, m, c, f, x, p, e and interned lookup tables verbs, mods, cats, files, extras, plus fileVersions aligned to files ('' when unknown); e is 0/1. idx/<id>.desc.json is an array aligned to rows with whitespace collapsed and descriptions clipped to 220 chars (219 + '…'). Module files go to data/<id>/<file>.json. The console prints each source's cmdlet count and the total with elapsed ms.
How to test: Run `npm run index`; build=$(jq -r .build src/sources.generated.json); check `jq '.n|length' public/a/$build/idx/az.json` equals `jq length public/a/$build/idx/az.desc.json` and equals sources[az].count; verify no desc string exceeds 220 chars: `jq '[.[]|length]|max' public/a/$build/idx/graph.desc.json` <= 220.

User story: As a maintainer, I want all build artifacts under /a/<build>/ where <build> is a hash of their content so that deploys never mix files from different builds and unchanged data keeps the same URLs.
Expected behaviour: emit() writes into public/a/.staging and feeds path+NUL+content+NUL into a single sha256 in write order. After all sources, build = first 12 hex chars of the digest; .staging is renamed to public/a/<build>; old public/a/ content is removed at the start of the run. src/sources.generated.json is written with {build, total, sources:[{id,label,short,color,sample,extra,count,version}]}. The app's assetUrl builds /a/<build>/<segments> URL-encoding each path segment, and fetchAsset fails on non-2xx with status and path, so an old tab after a deploy gets 404 instead of another build's files. Running the build twice on unchanged data yields the same build id. public/a/ and src/sources.generated.json are gitignored.
How to test: Run `npm run index` twice; `jq -r .build src/sources.generated.json` identical both times and `ls public/a` shows exactly one 12-hex directory (no .staging). Modify one description in a scratch copy, rerun -> build id changes and old directory is gone.

Feature: Immutable caching of build artifacts on Vercel
User story: As a maintainer, I want hashed artifact URLs served with a long immutable cache so that repeat visitors never re-download unchanged index data.
Expected behaviour: vercel.json sets framework astro, buildCommand `npm run build` (which runs `npm run index` then `astro build`), outputDirectory dist, and a header rule for source /a/(.*) adding `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Other paths get no custom cache header.
How to test: `jq '.headers' vercel.json` shows the /a/(.*) rule. Against a deployment: `curl -sI https://<site>/a/<build>/idx/az.json | grep -i cache-control` -> 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'; `curl -sI https://<site>/` does not have that value.

Feature: npm scripts for index, dev, build and verify
User story: As a maintainer, I want npm scripts that always regenerate the index before dev/build and a single verify gate so that local runs and CI use the same steps.
Expected behaviour: `npm run index` runs scripts/build-index.ts with node --experimental-strip-types (no TS build step). `dev` and `build` run index first. `typecheck` runs tsc --noEmit. `verify` = build && typecheck && playwright install --with-deps chromium && test:e2e (node tests/e2e.cjs); any step failing fails verify.
How to test: `jq .scripts package.json`; run `npm run index && npm run typecheck` and confirm exit 0 (do not run e2e here).

User story: As a maintainer, I want to refresh one source at a time into a temp directory and only replace data/<source>/ when its parser succeeds so that a failed run leaves committed data untouched and upstream deletions are reflected.
Expected behaviour: `bash pipelines/refresh.sh <id>` (missing arg -> usage error) sources pipelines/<id>/source.env for REPO, SPARSE and PARSE_DIR; clones into a mktemp dir (shallow --depth 1; with SPARSE non-empty uses --filter=blob:none --sparse and sparse-checkout set SPARSE; exchange has SPARSE=() so full shallow clone; az uses --no-cone 'azps-*/Az.*'). Runs parse_docs.py with PSINDEX_OUT=<tmp>/out and PYTHONPATH=pipelines on <docs>/<PARSE_DIR>. Under set -euo pipefail, any failure exits before `rm -rf data/<id>`; on success data/<id> is replaced wholesale by the new output. Temp dir removed on exit via trap. Parsers called without PSINDEX_OUT exit with 'PSINDEX_OUT is not set; run this parser through pipelines/refresh.sh <source>'.
How to test: `bash pipelines/refresh.sh` -> 'usage: pipelines/refresh.sh <source>'. `PYTHONPATH=pipelines python3 pipelines/az/parse_docs.py /tmp` -> exits with PSINDEX_OUT message. `bash pipelines/refresh.sh mecm` with network -> data/mecm replaced, `git status data/mecm` shows only changes from upstream. Simulate failure by setting REPO to an invalid URL in a scratch copy -> exit non-zero and data/mecm unchanged.

User story: As a maintainer, I want every manifest to record a known version string so that the UI never shows an unknown version and a failed lookup is visible but non-fatal when a prior version exists.
Expected behaviour: common.source_version(found, id): returns found if truthy; otherwise reads data/<id>/manifest.json 'v' (committed output) and, if present, prints `::warning::<id>: no version found this run; keeping the previous version <v>` and returns it; otherwise raises SystemExit `::error::<id>: no version found and none committed before`. Feature: Az module versions from the PowerShell Gallery rollup
User story: As a maintainer, I want each Az.* module's version taken from the Az rollup release's dependency list so that modules show real versions instead of the docs' 0.0.0 placeholder.
Expected behaviour: az parse_docs calls gallery_dependencies('Az', <rollup version>), fetching https://www.powershellgallery.com/api/v2/Packages(Id='Az',Version='<v>') with User-Agent PSIndex and 30 s timeout. parse_dependencies extracts <d:Dependencies> entries like 'Az.Accounts:[5.1.0, ):|Az.Advisor:3.0.0:' into {module: lower-bound version}; missing tag -> {}. Success prints '  Az <v>: <n> module versions from the PowerShell Gallery'. On URLError/OSError prints `::warning::Az <v>: PowerShell Gallery lookup failed (...); module versions left blank` and returns {}, so module files get version null (the build maps null to ''). Each modules/Az.<X>.json records version from this map.
How to test: `cd pipelines && python3 -c "import common; print(common.parse_dependencies('<d:Dependencies>Az.Accounts:[5.1.0, ):|Az.Advisor:3.0.0:</d:Dependencies>'))"` -> {'Az.Accounts': '5.1.0', 'Az.Advisor': '3.0.0'}; `python3 -c "import common; print(common.parse_dependencies('x'))"` -> {}. With network blocked, gallery_dependencies('Az','1.0.0') prints ::warning:: and returns {}.

Feature: Graph/Entra/Exchange module versions from the Gallery
User story: As a maintainer, I want Graph, Entra and Exchange module files to carry their latest Gallery versions with retries so that transient Gallery failures rarely blank versions.
Expected behaviour: graph and entra: fetch_module_version queries FindPackagesById(id) following 'next' pagination, returns the version flagged IsLatestVersion=true or None on any exception; fetch_all_module_versions runs 10 threads and retries failed modules up to 3 attempts, printing 'Resolved <found>/<n> module versions'. Exchange: queries latest non-prerelease version (orderby desc, top 1) per package in MODULE_PACKAGE_MAP with 15 s timeout, prints a warning per failure; modules without a mapping or failed lookup get version ''.
How to test: Run `bash pipelines/refresh.sh exchange` (network) and check `jq .version data/exchange/modules/ExchangePowerShell.json` is a version string; inspect logs for 'Resolved N/M module versions' on graph refresh.

User story: As a maintainer, I want each parser to write manifest.json, descriptions.json and modules/ in the shape the index build expects so that refreshed data indexes cleanly.
Expected behaviour: az: rows {n,v,m,c,e}, one file per Az.* module, skips module-index files and names not matching Verb-Az*, up to 3 examples with comment lines stripped. graph/entra: scan v1.0 and beta dirs, rows add a (api version 'v1.0'/'beta') and p, permissions in module files, Graph default description 'Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlet.' omitted from descriptions. exchange: six workload dirs (Exchange, Teams, Skype, Whiteboard, Office Web Apps, SharePoint Migration), missing dir is warned and skipped. mecm: rows {n,v,c,r(site role),e} without m, module files per category slug, parameters documented; exits 1 if the cmdlets dir is missing or no cmdlets parsed.

User story: As a maintainer, I want a refresh that lost more than 10% of a source's entries to be refused so that a failed clone or fetch cannot ship a partial dataset.
Expected behaviour: `python3 scripts/check-shrink.py <id> [ratio]` counts d entries in working-tree data/<id>/manifest.json vs `git show HEAD:data/<id>/manifest.json`. Prints '<id>: <old> -> <new> entries (<+/-pct>)'. If drop ratio > limit (default 0.10) prints `::error::<id> lost <k> entries (<pct> > 10%); refusing to commit a partial refresh` and exits 1. If no committed manifest exists, prints '<id>: no committed manifest, accepting <n> entries' and exits 0. Growth or drop <= limit exits 0. Old count 0 -> drop treated as 0. Versions are not checked.
How to test: In a scratch git clone, remove 20% of rows from data/az/manifest.json -> `python3 scripts/check-shrink.py az` exits 1 with ::error::. `python3 scripts/check-shrink.py az 0.5` exits 0. Restore and remove 5% -> exits 0. Unmodified -> '(+0.0%)' exit 0.

Feature: Daily and manual data refresh workflow planning
User story: As a maintainer, I want the data refresh to run daily and on demand for chosen sources so that data stays current and I can re-run just one source.
Expected behaviour: update-data.yml triggers on cron '17 5 * * *' and workflow_dispatch with input sources (default 'all'). The plan job sets sources to all pipelines/*/source.env ids when input is empty or 'all', otherwise splits the comma-separated input, strips whitespace and drops empty entries, outputting a JSON array. concurrency group update-data with cancel-in-progress false serializes runs. permissions: contents write.
How to test: Trigger via `gh workflow run update-data.yml -f sources='az, mecm'`; plan job output is ["az","mecm"] and only those refresh matrix jobs run. Locally simulate: `jq -cn --arg s 'az, ,mecm' '$s|split(",")|map(gsub("\\s";""))|map(select(length>0))'` -> ["az","mecm"].

User story: As a maintainer, I want each source refreshed and checked in its own job so that one source's upstream breakage does not block the others from shipping.
Expected behaviour: refresh job is a matrix over planned sources with fail-fast false and 30 min timeout. Steps: refresh.sh <source>; check-shrink.py <source>; `npm ci && npm run index` with the other sources as committed (so data the build rejects fails only that source); upload data/<source> as artifact data-<source> (3-day retention). A failing step means no artifact for that source. commit job runs if !cancelled() even when some matrix legs failed, downloads all artifacts, and for each refreshed/data-<src> replaces data/<src> wholesale (rm -rf then copy), echoing 'applied <src>'; nullglob makes zero artifacts a no-op.
How to test: Dispatch the workflow with an intentionally broken source (e.g. on a branch with an invalid REPO in pipelines/entra/source.env): entra leg fails, other legs upload artifacts, commit job still runs and logs 'applied az' etc. but not entra.

Feature: Verify gate before committing refreshed data
User story: As a maintainer, I want the combined refreshed data to pass the full build, typecheck and browser test suite before it is committed so that nothing ships to Vercel that breaks the site.
Expected behaviour: In the commit job, after applying artifacts, `npm ci && npm run verify` runs (build + typecheck + playwright chromium install + tests/e2e.cjs). If it fails the job fails before the Commit step, so nothing is committed or pushed. This compensates for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes not triggering ci.yml while Vercel still deploys them.
How to test: Inspect update-data.yml commit job step order: 'Build and test the refreshed site' precedes 'Commit'. On a run where e2e fails, confirm no 'chore(data)' commit appears on main.

Feature: Commit and push exactly the tested tree
User story: As a maintainer, I want the bot to commit only real data changes and push exactly the tree it tested so that main never receives untested data.
Expected behaviour: Commit step stages data/; if no staged diff prints 'No data changes.' and exits 0. Otherwise commit message is `chore(data): refresh <comma-separated changed source dirs>` (second path segment of changed files, sorted unique) authored and committed as github-actions[bot] <41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>, then `git push origin HEAD:<ref>`, with no pull/rebase; if main moved meanwhile the non-fast-forward push is rejected and the run fails, leaving the next run to refresh against the new main.
How to test: Check a bot commit on main: `git log --author='github-actions\[bot\]' -1 --format='%s %an'` -> 'chore(data): refresh az,graph github-actions[bot]'. A run with no upstream changes logs 'No data changes.' and creates no commit.

Feature: CI on pull requests and pushes to main
User story: As a maintainer, I want every PR and push to main to run the same verify gate as data refreshes so that code changes are tested against the committed data before merge.
Expected behaviour: ci.yml triggers on pull_request (any branch) and push to main; single job 'check' on ubuntu-latest, 15 min timeout: checkout, setup-node 22 with npm cache, npm ci, npm run verify. Any failure in build (including build-index validation/registry errors), typecheck or e2e fails the check.
How to test: Open a PR that adds an empty data/foo directory; the CI 'check' job fails at npm run verify with 'Source lists disagree'. A clean PR passes.

Feature: GitHub source link in the band
User story: As an admin, I want a link to the project's source from the header so that I can check how the index is built or report a problem.
Expected behaviour: The band's action group (data-quiet, next to the theme toggle) renders <a class="icon-btn" href="https://github.com/jorgeasaurus/PSIndex" aria-label="Source on GitHub"> containing an inline 18x18 GitHub mark SVG (aria-hidden). It is an ordinary link: no target, so it opens in the same tab, and the click is not intercepted.
How to test: Load /. Assert a[aria-label='Source on GitHub'] exists with href 'https://github.com/jorgeasaurus/PSIndex' and contains an svg[aria-hidden='true']. Click it and assert navigation to github.com.

Feature: Leading '/' is swallowed in an empty search box
User story: As an admin, I want pressing '/' while the empty search box already has focus to do nothing so that the focus shortcut never types a stray slash into my query.
Expected behaviour: Because the box is autofocused, the global '/' handler skips inputs. The box's own keydown handler instead prevents default for '/' when the input value is empty, so no '/' appears and no search runs. Once the box has text, '/' is typed normally (for example 'Get-/' stays as typed).
How to test: Load / (the input is focused). Press '/'. Assert input[aria-label='Search cmdlets'] value is ''. Type 'mg', then press '/'. Assert the value is 'mg/'.

Feature: Open entry marked in the result list
User story: As an admin, I want the row I opened to stay marked in the list so that I can see which result the detail pane is showing while I move the cursor elsewhere.
Expected behaviour: Each row whose key equals the open key (the open entry, or a deep-link key still being looked up) gets class is-open and aria-selected="true". Other rows have aria-selected="false". This is separate from the keyboard/hover cursor (.is-active): a row can be open without being active, and the reverse.
How to test: Search 'get-mguser' and click the first row. Assert that row has class 'is-open' and aria-selected='true'. Press ArrowDown and assert the second row is '.is-active' while the first row stays '.is-open'.

Feature: New search resets scroll and cursor; description refresh keeps your place
User story: As an admin, I want a new query to start at the top of its results, while the late arrival of descriptions does not throw me off the row I was on.
Expected behaviour: The cursor is stored as {search id, row ref}. When results arrive with a new id, the scroller goes to scrollTop 0 and the cursor falls back to index 0. When the worker re-runs the same search under the same id (after descriptions load), the scroll position is kept. If the cursor was set in that search, it follows its row to that row's new index and scrolls just enough to reveal it. If the row is gone, the cursor goes back to index 0.
How to test: Search 'user', scroll the list down, and type another character. Assert .results scrollTop is 0 and the first row is .is-active. To check refresh behaviour, throttle the idx/*.desc.json requests, press ArrowDown 3 times before they load, then assert the same cmdlet name is still .is-active after the descriptions arrive.

Feature: Worker runs only the latest search after the index loads
User story: As an admin typing quickly while the index is still loading, I want only my final query to be computed so that the first results show up as soon as possible.
Expected behaviour: Each 'search' message replaces lastSearch. Its run waits on the index promise and runs only if it is still lastSearch at that point, so searches that queued behind the load are dropped without being computed. Requests (rows, related, find) are not coalesced and are answered in arrival order once the index loads.
How to test: Throttle the idx/*.json shard requests and type 'g', 'ge', 'get' in turn before they finish. Assert only one results message is posted (for id 3), for example by instrumenting worker postMessage or checking that .count shows the 'get' results with no intermediate flashes.

User story: As an admin on a flaky connection, I want search to keep working on names when the description files fail to load so that a partial outage doesn't block lookups.
Expected behaviour: loadDescriptions catches any fetch failure of idx/<id>.desc.json and leaves that source's desc/ldesc null. No load-error is posted. Name-based matching still works, description matching (score 60) is skipped for that source, and its rows show the module name in place of a description. Other sources' descriptions are unaffected.
How to test: Block requests matching /a/*/idx/graph.desc.json. Load / and search 'mguser'. Assert results render, there is no role=alert, and Graph rows show the .result-module text in .result-desc.

Feature: Requests go unanswered after a failed index load
User story: As an admin, I want a failed index load to show one clear error and not a mix of half-working panels.
Expected behaviour: After the index promise rejects, the worker answers no searches or requests (both handlers swallow the rejection). SearchClient.request promises never settle, so a pending deep link, related list or Enter-open simply never resolves. The single load-error message drives the 'Index unavailable' count and the LoadFailed alert.
How to test: Block /a/*/idx/az.json and load /?c=graph:Get-MgUser. Assert role=alert shows 'The search index didn’t load.', .count reads 'Index unavailable', and no detail article ever renders.

User story: As an admin, I want the background field to react subtly to my pointer so that the page feels responsive without getting in the way.
Expected behaviour: A passive window pointermove listener records clientX/Y. Each frame, cells within 160px of the pointer get extra density of (1 - d/160) * 0.45 before the vertical falloff and quiet zones apply. The loop is capped at about 30 fps (frames less than 33ms apart are skipped) and the canvas resolution at devicePixelRatio 2. At most 8 ripples are kept (the oldest is dropped), and each fades out after 2.2s.
How to test: Load / with motion allowed and move the mouse over an empty part of the band. Compare canvas.field pixel data near the pointer before and after the move and assert more non-transparent glyph pixels near the pointer.
Code refs: src/app/ascii.ts:46, src/app/ascii.ts:72-77, src/app/ascii.ts:92, src/app/ascii.ts:129-134, src/app/ascii.ts:145, src/app/ascii.ts:169-170

User story: As an admin, I want selected text to use the current source's colour so that copying from the page matches the rest of the tinted UI.
Expected behaviour: ::selection uses a background of color-mix(in oklab, var(--src, var(--src-all)) 35%, transparent) and the normal text colour. Inside a row or detail article with its own --src, the selection takes that source's hue.
How to test: Open an Az entry, select text in .detail-desc, and check the computed ::selection background (or a screenshot) for the Az blue tint.

Feature: Syntax wraps only between parameters, with hanging indent and a narrow-screen fade
User story: As an admin reading a long parameter set, I want line breaks to fall between parameters and continuation lines to be indented so that each '-Name <Type>' stays readable.
Expected behaviour: Each top-level group (e.g. '[-Filter <String>]') renders as span.sg, a non-wrapping unit joined by single spaces, so lines break only between groups. .code-syntax pre uses padding-left 32px and text-indent -16px, which indents wrapped lines. At <=900px the syntax pre fades out over its last 28px (mask-image), the parameter table's Required column may wrap, and the detail title code shrinks to 21px.
How to test: Open graph:Get-MgUser at width 1280 and assert every span.sg has white-space nowrap. Resize to 390px and assert .code-syntax pre has a mask-image and .detail-title code font-size is 21px.

Feature: Short descriptions clipped for the index, full text in the detail
User story: As a maintainer, I want index descriptions kept short so that the description shards stay small while the detail pane still shows the full synopsis.
Expected behaviour: In buildShard, each row's description goes through clip(): runs of whitespace collapse to single spaces and the text is trimmed. If it is longer than 220 chars (DESC_MAX), it is cut to 219 chars, trailing space is trimmed and '…' is appended. Module files carry the unclipped descriptions.json text as `description`. A name missing from descriptions.json gets ''.
How to test: Run `npm run index`, then pick an entry with a long synopsis in data/<id>/descriptions.json. Assert its entry in public/a/<build>/idx/<id>.desc.json is at most 220 chars and ends with '…', and that public/a/<build>/data/<id>/<file>.json holds the full text.

User story: As a maintainer, I want the index build to print per-source counts and a total so that I can spot a source that came out empty or shrank.
Expected behaviour: For each source, the build logs a line with the id padded to 9 chars and the row count right-aligned in 6, followed by 'cmdlets'. It then logs '  <total> cmdlets indexed in <ms> ms'. Any thrown error is printed and the process exits 1.
How to test: Run `npm run index`. Assert stdout has one line per source (graph, az, entra, exchange, mecm) matching /^\s+\w+\s+\d+ cmdlets$/ and a final 'cmdlets indexed in N ms' line, with exit code 0.

Feature: Parsers refuse to run without PSINDEX_OUT
User story: As a maintainer, I want running a parser directly to fail loudly so that I never write over committed data/<source>/ by accident.
Expected behaviour: common.output_dir() raises SystemExit with 'PSINDEX_OUT is not set; run this parser through pipelines/refresh.sh <source>' when the environment variable is empty or unset. refresh.sh sets it to an empty mktemp directory, and parsers treat data/<id>/ as read-only (it is used only for the previous version).
How to test: Run `PYTHONPATH=pipelines python3 pipelines/mecm/parse_docs.py /tmp/x` without PSINDEX_OUT. Assert a non-zero exit and that message on stderr, with git status showing data/ unchanged.

Feature: Alternative PowerShell extractors from installed modules
User story: As a maintainer on Windows, I want to regenerate Az or MECM data from the installed modules, not from the docs repos, so that I can index a module version the docs don't cover yet.
Expected behaviour: pipelines/az/get-azcmdlets.ps1 (#Requires -Module Az, -OutputDir defaulting to the repo root) takes the newest of each installed Az.* module. It stops with 'No Az.* modules found. Install the Az module first: Install-Module Az' if there are none. The version comes from the Az rollup, else Az.Accounts, else '0.0.0'. It writes data\az\manifest.json ({v,d}), descriptions.json and modules\<Az.Module>.json. pipelines/mecm/get-mecmcmdlets.ps1 (-OutputPath defaulting to data\mecm, optional -ModulePath) locates ConfigurationManager.psd1. If it can't, it errors with 'ConfigurationManager module not found. Install the MECM admin console or specify -ModulePath' and exits 1. It writes manifest.json, descriptions.json and one modules\<category>.json per category, and shows progress every 50 cmdlets.
How to test: On a Windows host with Az installed, run `pwsh pipelines/az/get-azcmdlets.ps1` and assert data/az/manifest.json has a 'v' and a non-empty 'd', then run `npm run index` and assert it succeeds. Run get-mecmcmdlets.ps1 without the console installed and assert exit 1 with the 'module not found' message.

Feature: Serialised data refresh runs and short-lived artifacts
User story: As a maintainer, I want only one data refresh running at a time so that a manual dispatch and the daily cron never race to push to main.
Expected behaviour: update-data.yml declares concurrency group 'update-data' with cancel-in-progress false, so a second run queues behind the active one and is not cancelled. The workflow has contents: write permission. Each source's refreshed data/<source> is uploaded as artifact 'data-<source>' with retention-days 3.
How to test: Inspect .github/workflows/update-data.yml: assert concurrency.group == 'update-data', concurrency.cancel-in-progress == false, permissions.contents == 'write', and the upload-artifact step has name 'data-${{ matrix.source }}' and retention-days 3. Dispatch two runs back to back and confirm in the Actions UI that the second waits.
